message.content:
You are skeptic #2. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "admin-reports" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/components/admin/ReportCard.tsx
LOCATION: Lines 83-91 (Review button conditional rendering)
RULE: 4
TITLE: Conditional button visibility may break keyboard navigability
DETAIL: The 'Review' button only renders if report.status === 'open' (line 82). While logically correct, this means a keyboard user tabbing through a reviewed report will suddenly skip where a button would be, creating inconsistent tab order across different report cards. The button is appropriately disabled on pending actions via the 'pending' state, but complete removal causes cognitive discontinuity.
SUGGESTION: Either (a) always render both buttons, disabling 'Review' for reviewed reports and 'Suspend' for targetless reports (better keyboard continuity), or (b) add aria-label to the card explaining why a button is absent. Current approach is acceptable but option (a) improves keyboard UX.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

The tab order skips the non-existent button naturally - A screen reader user will navigate from one card's available buttons to the next card's available buttons, which is semantically correct **Comparison to UsersTable pattern:** - Line 52-56 in UsersTable: Also renders conditionally, but uses `—` as a placeholder - However, that placeholder is NOT a button and NOT in tab order - So the "better UX" argument (always render, disable button) would create a DISABLED button in the tab order **Actual accessibility concern:** - The finding claims "cognitive discontinuity" — but there's no logical inconsistency in tab order - The buttons that CAN exist DO exist; those that shouldn't DON'T appear - Disabling a button that can never be used (Review a reviewed report) would be semantically misleading - The current design is actually more honest: if you can't review a report that's already reviewed, don't show a disabled button pretending you could **Test evidence:** - The test at line 28-37 runs `axe(container)` and expects NO violations - This already covers keyboard navigation and accessibility **Verdict:** This is a **stylistic opinion**, not a genuine accessibility gap.
